full_text: How long can one marathon take? You're off by about 54 years. 1912. Shizo Kanakuri, one of Japan's first two Olympians ever, travels 18 days by ship and rail to run the Stockholm marathon. The race is so hot that one runner dies. Sixteen miles in, Kanakuri staggers off the course - into a stranger's garden party, where he drinks orange juice for an hour. Too ashamed to tell anyone, he quietly goes home to Japan. So Sweden lists him as a missing person. For fifty years. In 1967, Swedish television finds him - alive, 75 years old. They invite him back to finish his race. He crosses the line at 54 years, 8 months, 6 days, 5 hours, 32 minutes, and 20.3 seconds. Afterwards, he said it had been a long trip. Along the way, he got married, had six children, and ten grandchildren.
